verdict: Berkshire's operating earnings jumped 71% to $14.5B as insurance underwriting quadrupled to $3.4B — and $6.6B of investment gains lifted headline profit to $19.7B, though that was still only half of a year ago's $37.6B, when the stock portfolio soared.

footerNote: Berkshire has no single gross-profit line: costs are split following the 10-K's own structure. Fourth-quarter figures are full-year 2024 results from the 10-K minus the first nine months of 2024 as restated in the Q3 2025 10-Q. Berkshire reclassified some businesses between its Insurance and Other and Railroad, Utilities and Energy sections in 2024, so no year-ago growth rate is shown for the sales-and-service, utility and service revenue lines.
follow100Note: Paper gains on the stock portfolio added $6.90 of every $100 of revenue — without them, the businesses and everything else kept $13.85. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Underwriting quadrupled
takeaways.text: After-tax underwriting earnings rose to $3.4B from $0.8B a year ago, led by GEICO: higher average premiums per policy, lower claims frequencies and improved efficiency took GEICO's full-year pre-tax underwriting profit to $7.8B. Hurricane losses from Helene and Milton were about $360M at GEICO.

takeaways.title: Operating earnings jumped 71%
takeaways.text: The businesses themselves earned $14.5B after tax, up from $8.5B — insurance investment income rose to $4.1B after tax on the bigger cash pile, and 'Other' earnings got a roughly $1.2B boost from currency gains on foreign-denominated debt.

takeaways.title: The float kept growing
takeaways.text: Insurance float — the premiums Berkshire holds and invests before claims come due — reached about $171B at year-end, up $2B in the year. Berkshire also sold down investments during 2024, realizing about $79.6B of after-tax gains, much of it from trimming Apple.

oneTimers: Investment gains of $6,552M before tax are mostly paper gains. Of the after-tax investment gains of $5,167M, about $2.1B was an increase in unrealized gains on stocks Berkshire still owns and $3.1B was realized gains on stocks sold. Next quarter the unrealized part can just as easily reverse — a year ago this line was $29.1B after tax, which is why headline profit then was $37.6B.

Currency gains on foreign debt: revaluing Berkshire's euro-, pound- and yen-denominated borrowings produced a gain of about $1.2B after tax in the quarter, versus a loss of about $684M a year ago. It sits inside the 'Other' operating earnings line and flatters the 71% jump.

sources.label: Form 10-Q, quarter ended September 30, 2025 — restated 2024 comparatives (SEC EDGAR)
